initial:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: 16-pose transparent cinematic sprite sheet for Óscar D'León's single fighting-game entrance.
Input image 1: the existing Oscar cinematic atlas locks his identity, costume and hand-painted retro game illustration style. Preserve his bald head, thick dark moustache, warm dark brown skin, expressive face, black satin open overshirt, black tiger-print T-shirt, gold necklace, sparkly black trousers and black loafers.
Primary request: replace the wide-arm static turn with a lively single action: he takes a wireless microphone from inside his jacket, raises it to his mouth and performs as if singing, then does ONE compact salsa spin on his feet, lowers/stows the mic and returns to guard. The microphone must be clearly visible and held by the SAME anatomical RIGHT hand throughout, never swapped between hands. It has a silver mesh head and short black handle. Singing expression: mouth open and engaged, left hand expressive; microphone just in front of mouth, not covering his face.
Composition: exactly SIXTEEN isolated full-body poses in FOUR equal columns and FOUR equal rows, chronological left-to-right top-to-bottom, genuine transparent alpha. Consistent scale and planted-foot baseline, generous gaps, complete heads/hands/shoes, no neighboring silhouettes touching. Prefer 2048x2048 or larger. Every pose is the SAME recognizable man.
Frame chronology:
0 original relaxed fighting guard facing three-quarter RIGHT, hands empty.
1 right hand reaches into the inside jacket near his chest, left hand gently opens.
2 right hand draws out the wireless microphone at chest height.
3 right hand raises microphone to mouth, face turned slightly toward camera.
4 joyful singing gesture, microphone at mouth, left palm reaching toward audience, knees soft.
5 finish the singing gesture and prepare the turn, nearly front-facing, mic still near chin.
6 start compact salsa pivot, three-quarter FRONT facing LEFT, left elbow relaxed.
7 strict LEFT profile, feet pivoting, microphone still in right hand near upper chest.
8 three-quarter BACK facing LEFT, jacket swings naturally, right hand microphone remains attached.
9 full BACK view (back of bald head, plain jacket back), halfway through turn.
10 three-quarter BACK facing RIGHT, continuing same direction.
11 strict RIGHT profile, foot crossing into final half of turn.
12 three-quarter FRONT facing RIGHT, face visible again, mic near chest.
13 completes ONE revolution into front-facing stance, small celebratory left-hand flourish.
14 turns slightly to original RIGHT-facing opponent stance, right hand lowering microphone toward inside jacket.
15 original RIGHT-facing fighting guard, microphone stowed and hands empty.
The spin uses anatomically correct front/profile/back views, never a flat cutout rotation or mirrored copies. Keep dancing compact and charismatic rather than both arms spread throughout. No added characters, stage, floor, shadows, numbers, labels, grid, musical notes or special effects.
